evidence: src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: export function errorHandler(error: unknown, _req, res, _next) is Express error middleware that maps errors to HTTP JSON responses.
src/infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts: function statusFor(error: DomainError) is the only place where domain errors are mapped to HTTP statuses (400/404/409/422).
src/infrastructure/http/middleware/notFoundHandler.ts: export function notFoundHandler(req, res) sends a 404 with code 'ROUTE_NOT_FOUND', the same kind of HTTP error response.
Both files send the same response body { error: { code, message } }, a minor inline repetition rather than a duplicated invariant.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with the same thing: Express terminal middleware that turns failures into HTTP error responses. errorHandler.ts maps thrown DomainError subclasses, malformed JSON and unexpected errors to status codes and a JSON error body. notFoundHandler.ts produces the 404 for requests that match no route. Both use the same abstraction, plain Express (req, res) handlers. Neither bypasses anything in the module, and both send the same { error: { code, message } } body. The domain-error-to-status mapping lives in one place, statusFor in errorHandler.ts. The body literal is written out in four places (three in errorHandler.ts, one in notFoundHandler.ts). That is a small repeated pattern, not a business rule or invariant copied in two places. A shared helper could factor it out, but this does not reach the rubric's fail bar.
